title: Keys To Living Above The Storm
paragraphs: You have heard this topic throughout this meeting because the next year of your life, 2012, is going to be a stormy year and we need to understand the nature of storms. I want to focus on how to cope with a changing environment, and that's what storms represent. Storms change everything; nothing remains the same. And you guys, listen carefully tonight as we go over this topic. I'm going to move on very quickly, but I want you to get a copy of this CD.

And to our friends in Freeport, our sister church there, this word is for everyone sitting in that crowded place there in Freeport. I want to start with a few phrases that I want you to write down. First and foremost, write this down. The greatest commodity that all of humanity possesses on Earth is time. What is surprising about time is that everyone has the same amount. Many of us do not have the same amount of money, but we all have the same amount of time. 24 hours a day.

Time is what I call the currency of life. Currency is what you use to buy things. You have heard the term "spending time". This is a true principle. We spend time. What you are now was bought with the time you spent. What you are now, your life. In other words, what you will become in this new year 2012 will be determined by how you spend your time. We are about to change time. We are about to move on to another period of our lives.

What is surprising is that everything you used your time for in 2011 is what you have become today. I believe that the greatest protection against wasting time is planning. Let everyone say: planning. The way you control your time is through planning. Why? Because the plan is the way you control time. You can't really stop time. You can't even save it. But you can control it. You control the time by making a plan. The plan tells you how to spend your time. Without a plan, time is wasted.

Many of you, when you look back on 2011, feel a lot of regret for not using and spending your time properly. This could be because you didn't make a plan, or you didn't stick to the plan, or you forgot the plan. Let me assure you then that every new year is an act of fate. It gives you a new pen and a blank page from the pages of life. This is the meaning of the new year. It is time that gives you another blank page.

And fate says that it is now your responsibility to determine what the next chapter of your life will look like. We know what 2012 looked like. It's over. Perhaps your semester there wasn't as successful as you had hoped. But I tell you that this new year is God giving you once again a blank sheet of paper and a pen. He stands on the threshold of a new year and says to you: "Write again." What the end of this new year will look like depends entirely on you. Please write this down. God has a plan for your life.

That's why God has plans for your life—because He knows that without a plan, you'll waste your time. And every year is a chapter in God's plan for your life. I think we need to focus intensely on planning for this new year. And I mean planning it now because the year is going to be very turbulent. It's going to be so chaotic that if you don't have a plan for 2012, you'll be tossed about by the winds of change. Some of you will actually lose your minds. You will lose your sanity. You will lose your marriages.

You will lose your homes. You will lose your cars. You will lose your health if you don't align yourselves with God's plan. This is a phrase I found very important in the book of Jeremiah when I was thirteen, and it still guides my life today. Jeremiah 29:11 says, "For I know the thoughts I have for you." Thoughts of peace, not evil, to give you a future and a hope. "Plans give you hope and a future. Then, when you have a plan, you can call on me. This means only call on me if you have the plan properly in place.

Why? Because when you call on me, you will call on me according to the plan to do what I said I planned to do for you. And then I will listen to you. This means that if you don't have a plan, God doesn't listen. Then I will hear you. He says, ' You will seek me and find me.' When you seek me with all your hearts, I will appear to you and be found by you, says the Lord, and I will restore your captivity.

Many of us today are enslaved to banks, enslaved to people we have borrowed money from, and enslaved to certain organizations that have become our source of income. And God says, 'If you follow my plan, I will set you free from bondage.' I will deliver you from slavery." When we talk about plans, we have to talk about these storms that we have to face. 2011 will be a year of storms. Let everyone say: The storm.

You will remember that I said this, I promise you that April is going to be a very stormy month for some of us. You will remember. I remember what Dr. Monroe said that night, that there would be some storms in September. There will be more storms. And I tell you prophetically that the hurricane season and the stormy season of life are about to hit us. What I like about this expression, hurricane season, is that we use it here in the Caribbean, but I like it because it means that it is not always.

In fact, stormy seasons mean that storms come and go. A hurricane is a storm. A storm is a crisis. Let me introduce you to the storm. You might want to write this down. A storm is a temporary gathering of natural currents and elements that interact with and affect the environment, changing the normal course of life. This is the storm. Let me repeat it because you will feel this throughout the year in 2012.

It is a temporary gathering of natural currents and elements that interact with and affect the environment and disrupt the natural course of life. Now notice that the word "natural" is present in this definition. Another definition: A storm is a collision of known elements in unexpected ways. In other words, the storm is a test of tradition through the unexpected. Storms are a natural occurrence. It is a collection of natural things that already exist. Storms don't come from outer space.

Any hurricane is something that came directly from the ground. A tsunami comes from the earth. Tropical cyclones originate from the Earth's elements. A hurricane is wind, water, and heat. She is always here. We love the wind when it cools the weather for us. We love water when it quenches our thirst. We love the rain when it brings the plants to life. But when they come together in a unique way, they can kill us. In other words, a storm is always a combination of natural elements working together in a unique way.

This means that storms are not unusual. So what do you do when everything you trusted collapses in a storm? How do you prepare for a sudden change in your life? And how do you recover when life surprises you from where you least expect it? And some of you know that feeling very well. What do you do after a lifetime of hard work, dedication, commitment, and loyalty? How do your career and skills suddenly change when you are laid off from your job? When all the skills you have learned are no longer required.

What do you do when the ground is pulled out from under your feet, as we all know happens to many people? How do you face the family you once left, only to return to them because you couldn't pay the rent or mortgage, and were forced to live with your parents again? How do you deal with these types of problems? Many of the people sitting in this room today, and the thousands watching this program, will tell you that they had this experience in the past year. I tell you, things are going to get worse in 2012.

Look at the people in Grand Bahama watching this program today. Can you imagine that two days before New Year's Day they were laid off from their jobs? It couldn't get any worse. Well, there are people sitting here who have been through and are going through horrible things. But what I like about life is that God says that as long as the earth remains, there will be planting and harvesting, cold and heat, summer and winter, night and day, and it will never end. Let everyone say "daytime". Let everyone say "night".

Let everyone say summer. Let everyone say winter. God says that as long as the earth remains, there will be a time for sowing and a time for reaping. There will be dark nights, but there will be days after them. There will be winter. It will be cold, but I promise you, he says, there will be summer. Clap for God for some hope in life. In Ezekiel chapter 34, God says, “I will bless the people and the places around my hill.” Keep an eye on him. I will descend upon you.

Rain in its proper time, and what will it be rain of? Blessings. Take a breath. Some of you kept believing that God would bless you all the time. But according to this text, did God say that you will receive blessings all the time? Oh, my God. How does blessing come about? Read it aloud. Come on, be honest. In due time. Some of you are in a season of abundance right now. The others are bankrupt. But let me tell you something about the seasons. If you are broke now, I guarantee you won't be broke forever.

It's just a season of bankruptcy. Is this a new word? If you are sick now, it is sickness season. Use your faith and say, "God, I will get through this season." On the other hand, this disease will be replaced by good health and a strong body. What will be the rains in? In the seasons. He says: "In other words, the seasons are controlled by God." This makes me feel very comfortable, because whether it rains or the sun shines, God is in control. Please write this down.

The greatest blessing in life is that life is seasonal. Ecclesiastes 3 says: "There is a season for everything." There is a time for everything under heaven. " In other words, everything is seasonal." This means that no matter what you go through, it cannot last. Seasons are important because they ensure change. The seasons bring hope. Nothing stays the same during the season. Seasons are always temporary. The key to survival is to hold on until the end of the season.

In other words, the seasons provide an incentive to plan for the future because you know that winter cannot last. So don't throw away your summer clothes. Is anyone here? When it gets cold, don't throw away your swim trunks. Why? Because you know there is a future after the cold. In other words, the seasons are always changing. Never give permanent results to a temporary problem. This is very important because when you are in a dark moment, you sometimes think that it is your permanent address.

But never make a permanent decision to try to solve a temporary problem. This is what happens in divorce cases. Often in marriage, you go through a very difficult moment. I mean, hell on earth. And believe me, you have a choice. Will I make a permanent decision at this stage, or will I persevere through this season and get through this dark moment? This happens with friendships. It even happens with jobs. This happens with businesses. Sometimes you want to quit your job. Life is extremely difficult.

But everything is seasonal. This is the source of encouragement in life. When you see a storm coming, I want you to understand the nature of storms. Please write this down. That's a very modern vision for me. First and foremost, storms are natural. Let everyone say it's normal. Storms are a natural occurrence. Secondly, storms are temporary. There is no permanent hurricane. There is no permanent earthquake. There is no permanent tsunami. There is no permanent hurricane. They are all temporary.

Third, storms are always moving. Hurricanes, you hear them talking about them moving at 7 miles per hour, or 10 miles, or five, they are moving. Every storm in life is in motion. This leads me to point five. Storms force change. Fourth, storms force change. This is important. Storms force you to change. There is a tree in my yard that was beautiful before the hurricane hit us this year. When the hurricane hit, my tree disappeared. Oh my God. I miss my tree. So, I had to get used to the absence of this tree.

The tornado knocked down the top of the tree. Storms force change. This leads me to point five. Storms restore nature to its original state. Some people were overweight until the doctor said, "Come on, everyone. Anyone who can listen to me. You know you've been eating too much. You know you've been overweight. Look, if you don't lose 20 pounds in six weeks, you're going to die." "Suddenly, you stop eating everything. Why? What does the storm do? It brings you back to your normal state.

Your body says, based on your height and bone structure, you should weigh 125, but you weigh 200. So the storm comes with a heart attack and problems with your lungs and liver, and suddenly your body says, 'Look, put me back where I was.' Don't curse the storm. It comes to bring you back to your senses. Sixth, storms reveal weaknesses. There are some trees that look good until a hurricane comes. You know those trees? They look beautiful, strong, and big.

Suddenly, when they fall, you see that inside they were rotten. There are people like that in this place. They look good. But when life hits them, suddenly and unexpectedly, everything you thought they were strong about is exposed. Storms confirm how strong you are. No matter how much you claim to have faith, storms will test whether you have it or not. Storms bring you back to God. That's why they come." Storms. They come to bring you back to God.

Some people become very arrogant, earning a lot of money and owning all these things. Suddenly, boom, God says, "Thank you very much." " The storm comes to bring you back directly to God. Number nine, storms restore true values. I heard testimony tonight about someone having a gun to their head and calling out the most precious thing in their life. Half the things you own, you do n't use. And the other half, you don't want. One pillow, one plate, a fork, a spoon, and a knife, a pot, and some food. That's it.

You don't need a television in every room. You're hardly ever home to watch them anyway. Come on, let's talk about this for a minute. You see, the storm will come to tell you what's truly precious again, like your wife and children. I heard about a man who was sick this year. I spoke to him yesterday. He said, ' Doctor, I'm at home with my children.'" He said, "You don't understand. I was on the brink of death in October, and I promised God that this Christmas I wouldn't go anywhere.

I could kiss my grandchildren again. I could talk to my son again, and he's 35. I'd spend time with my daughter, and she's 42. Why? They suddenly became precious to me because I was dead. The storm will bring you back to what 's important. Don't curse the storm. And in 2012, God will bring you back to what's important. And number 10, write it down. Storms remind us of our mortality. Storms will tell you that you will die. Some people have just survived a storm.

You're sitting here today, some of you by the grace of God. I mean, what you went through in 2012 and 2011, rather, you were on the brink of death and you survived. The storm will only remind you that you are not all that. That's why every time I meet a cocky person, I say to myself, ' Father (God) will take care of that.' There are some people They think they don't need anyone. Don't worry about that. He'll take care of everything. So don't pretend to be cold here. I won't clap. I won't sing. You'd better sing.

You're not that cold, brother. That's why God brings storms into our lives, to bring us back to our mortality. To make us realize that we won't be here forever. That's right. I was talking to Sister Andre. She's here tonight. I said to her, " Andre, your father died a few days before the New Year." Can you imagine that? He didn't make it to the next year." I said, " But he lived a good life." He dedicated his life to our country. " You have no reason to be ashamed." He was a strong man who served our country.

Sir Clifford, my dear, I wonder what you are doing. A storm will come to remind you that of all you gain, you will take nothing with you but a coffin. And all those clothes you are so proud of, there are those waiting for you to die to wear them. So you had better straighten up in 2012 and get back to what is important. It is people, God, family, and worship. Number 11, write this down. Storms break pride. There are some people here, you know, who weren't used to talking to you. But they are talking now. Why?

The job is gone, life has changed, the car is gone, it's all over. Suddenly they are not so haughty anymore. Storms will lower your pride. Tell your neighbor, stay humble. And number 12, write this down. Storms turn you toward God. They bring you back to the divine. I heard today on CNN, the meteorologist appeared. He said that 2011 was a terrible year for the world in terms of natural disasters. And then he said at the end, I wonder if Man will one day be able to control nature. No, never.

That house you spent all that money on. The roof's gone. Where did that roof go? Oh Lord, the roof flew off. Life is that fragile. That's why 2012 should be a year you learn how to handle storms. Write this down. The ten purposes of a storm. What is a storm for? Number one, it comes to restore natural balance. Number two, it comes to cleanse the environment. Number three, it comes to remove pollution. There are people in your life that storms will sweep away.

Some people are only with you because you have money now. But when the storm of breaking hits, everyone leaves. And that's when you find out who your real friends are. Everyone here applauds. You know who I'm talking about. Suddenly, they're all gone. I call them pollution. Every time a hurricane leaves the Bahamas, the air is clear. The wind is clean. The water is beautiful. Why? Because hurricanes come to clean up pollution. Number four, storms come to expose decay. Number five, they come to test your strength.

Number six, they come to keep you humble. Number seven, Storms come to reduce life to its essentials. Number eight, storms come to test your foundation. A woman told me recently, "Father Miles, I've been without electricity for five months." I said, "What?" "She said, 'Yes.' And added, 'I've finally gotten used to using lamps and candles.' I said, ' My dear,' and she said, 'Don't pity me.' She had forgotten what it felt like to read by the light of a kerosene lamp. God will allow storms to bring you back to basics.

Don't curse the storm. Number eight, storms come to test your foundations. Number nine, they come to test the standards of your construction. Oh my God. Oh my God. There are so many houses in the Bahamas that weren't built to standard. You know some of them. And when hurricanes come, they immediately expose them. They're the first thing to collapse. Your life is just like that. If you're not built to God's standards, then when the storms of life come, we'll see you exposed.

Number ten, storms come to give you a key. What is that key? I've found a key. Matthew 16:19 says, ' What will I give you? The keys of the kingdom of heaven. Whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth will be loosed in heaven.' Then it says, ' I will give you the secrets of the Kingdom of God. You alone will possess the secrets of the ability to control the Earth's environment. He is talking about the people of the Kingdom.

Let's talk about one of these keys that I want to share with you today. Matthew 7 says this. Therefore, everyone who hears these words of mine and acts upon them is like a wise man who built his house on what? The rock. Then the rain came down, the rivers came, and the winds blew and struck that house, but it did not fall. Why? Because it was founded on rock. Now, I want you to review the following verse.

But everyone who hears these words of mine and does not act upon them is like a foolish man who also built his house, but on sand. Then the rain came down, the rivers came, the winds blew and struck that house, and it fell, and its fall was great. Now, this is the point I want you to learn from this. Jesus Christ is saying something very important here. First of all, storms are a natural part of life. He says, look, it's coming for everyone.

Sometimes we think we are committing a sin because things have become difficult. No, no. Storms come whether you make a mistake or not. Whether built on sand or rock, storms come to both houses. Write this down. Secondly, storms should be expected. Christ was saying, Look, whether you are in a secure house or a shaky one, the storm does not care. She's coming. Storms are expected. Third, storms come to everyone. Sometimes we think we are very unique. I'm the only one going through this.

Listen, you don't understand. The people behind you have problems that are ten times worse than yours. Everyone will face storms. This is what Christ says. Whether you are built on rock or sand, storms will confront you. Fourth, storms affect everyone. Fifth, storms are not the core of the problem in life. I thought it was important to remember, because if storms hit everyone, the storm itself is not the issue. Let me say it slowly. If the storm hits everyone, storms are not the main issue in life.

Don't worry about the storm. She's coming anyway. You need to focus on something else. In other words, storms come to reveal what they were built on. Therefore, the most important thing in life in 2012 is not the number of storms coming. You should focus on whether you are built the right way. In other words, the structure is more important than the storm. That's why God brought you here tonight. He brought you here to tell you that there will be many storms and very frequent storms in 2012.

But I will give you the key. He says the key to overcoming life's storms is to secure your building standards, your foundation, and the materials you've built with. I have no fear of storms. There is nothing to fear in 2012. Why? Because the storm is not the problem. The problem is whether I am built on the right foundation and have the right materials and standards. If you don't have the right things, he says there will be a great collapse. It will collapse and fall apart.

In other words, you are never reminded of what you avoided in life. You remind us of what endured and survived. Never trust someone who hasn't weathered any storm. I will never forget when I read Bill Gates' book. I will never forget him. They asked Mr. Gates, "How?" They asked him, "What's the secret to your success at Microsoft?" He said, "The managers." They asked, " How do you hire managers?" He said, "I interview them myself." They asked, "What's the process?"

He said, "Well, I interview the managers and ask them the basic questions." He said, "But there's one question I save for last, and if they answer it correctly, I hire them. If they answer incorrectly, I don't hire them." They asked, "What's the question?" He said, " The question I always ask them is this: Have you ever failed before? Have you ever made a mistake? Have you ever experienced a career collapse?" He said, "If they say no, I don't hire them."

He says: "I don't trust anyone who hasn't been through a storm." "Why? Because you're not remembered for what you avoided. How do we know David? Goliath. How do we know Joshua? The Wall. How do we know Samson? The Philistines. How do we know Moses? Pharaoh. If you don't have problems, you don't have a reputation. What made Mandela famous? Jail time. What made Martin Luther King Jr. famous? Jail time, marches, and dogs. Listen, why do n't you give yourself a great chance to become famous next year?

Invite some storms into your life and show them how strong you are. Just show them that I will survive, and after I do everything, I will still survive. Never trust someone who hasn't survived anything. Everyone can bribe, but few can testify. Let me tell you something. The eagle. The eagle is the only bird that seeks out storms, and it's the only bird that God identified with. The eagle is an unusual bird, and it's the king of birds. Here's why.

First, the eagle is the king of birds because the eagle understands storms. Second, third, the eagle seeks out storms. It's the only bird that seeks out storms." In the desert, you see an eagle soaring high in search of storms— sandstorms and tornadoes. Why? Because eagles welcome storms. Why? Because eagles fly toward storms when they see them. Now, why do they do that? The answer is quite simple. The eagle uses the storm to increase its altitude. Number seven, the eagle uses the storm to rest.

An eagle's wingspan can reach seven feet. When an eagle sees a storm, it enters it. It lets the storm's current lift it upward. Then it spreads its wings and rests above the storm. When the storm arrives, the eagle rests. I am an eagle. Number eight, the eagle uses the storm to clean its feathers. All the dust in the desert gets trapped in the feathers, so the eagle enters the storm, and the wind speed washes away that dust. In other words, it uses the storm for purification.

The eagle also uses the storm to test its wings. That's the ossuary, a small bone in its wing that it attaches. It has to test it in the storm to see if it's secure, and then it rests. And number ten, eagles let the storm pass when they're done using it. In the year 2012, I want you to use every storm that comes. Someone say Amen here. And I want you to say to the storm: I will use you to grow in faith. I will prove my faith on you. I will rest in the Lord, who is the Lord of the storm.

And when I have finished using you, I will let you go on your way. That is why you must learn how storms work. Eagles are not afraid of storms. And I challenge you to be like eagles because eagles are the most successful birds in the world. Now, let me conclude with this. Nothing is permanent except God. We must settle this for 2012. God promises us that nothing is permanent, only God is permanent. Look at Ecclesiastes again. God says that everything has a time and a season. This means that nothing is forever.

If you have a lot now, it is not forever. If you have nothing now, it is not forever. If you are on top now, it is not forever. If you are at the bottom now, it is not forever. Everything is seasonal. So there is no need to panic in The seasons. You have to find something that doesn't change. There are two things that don't change. First, God, and second, His promises. But the problem is that God's promises do change. So His promises are true, including the one that says nothing stays the same.

Thus, God has a plan for your life. And I assure you, my friends, that God does not change. Look at James 1:16. Write it down. It says, "Do not be deceived, my beloved brothers and sisters. Every good gift and every perfect gift— where does it come from? From above, from the Father of lights, with whom there is no change, nor shadow of turning. He is eternal." Another verse, Psalm 145:13, says, "Your kingdom, O God, is an everlasting kingdom." " And your dominion endures to every generation."

The Lord is faithful to all his promises and loves all that he has made. God says, " My promises are firm." I love this verse. James 1:2 rather. He says, "Consider it pure joy, my brothers." When you face storms, of all kinds, because you know, it's truly amazing. The only way to face storms with joy is to know something. If you don't know something, you can't be joyful in the storm. What should you know? First, he says that you need to know that the test of your faith creates what? patience.

And patience must have a complete role in your lives, so that you may be perfect and complete, lacking nothing. The only way to live a life without flaws is to be tested by storms. He says: "Feel pure joy when it comes, because you know that this storm will make you better people, stronger, and more patiently steadfast." Can I hear Amen? Tell the person next to you, I am in a school of patience now. In other words, don't leave the classroom. Stay in the classroom until patience has done its full work.

Ladies and gentlemen, Deuteronomy 32 says: “The Lord’s portion is his people.” He protected him and took care of him. He protected him like the pupil of his eye. Like an eagle, it moves its nest, hovers over its chicks, and spreads its wings to carry them on its feathers. The Lord alone will guide you. Listen, eagles only use their feathers in a storm. God says, " I will carry you on my feathers," meaning that God will let you fall into the storm and then pick you up, as he says. But he will not let the storm pass.

He will be with you in the storm, and together you will use the storm to rise higher. He says he will put you on his feathers, and show you how to use your own feathers. He will personally train you on how to deal with storms. He went through the experiences so that you could go through them too. Can I hear Amen? Now, let me put it very simply for you. In Luke 22, Jesus says, “Simon, behold, Satan has demanded to sift you like wheat, but I have prayed for you, that your faith may not fail.”

When you return, strengthen your brothers. In other words, you are not eligible to help anyone until you get over something. He said to Peter, "Tell your neighbor; you know nothing until you experience something." "Hit him." Tell them again: "You don't know anything until you experience something." "If you pass by something, clap your hands." Thank God that you emerged from your experience unscathed. I'm going to put an end to this tonight. 10 keys to rising above the storm.

Write these keys down and keep them in your front door, on your refrigerator, and at your workplace. This is what I use to get through my storms. First, believe that you were made for storms. The eagle believes it is capable of handling the storm. He was created for her. Secondly, know that storms are a natural phenomenon. Stop being amazed because things are difficult. Can I say that again? Stop being amazed because things are difficult. Stop being shocked that you lost your job.

Stop being surprised because your business is going through a tough time. Why? Storms are a natural occurrence. Third, you must understand the nature of storms. That's why I'm teaching her tonight. Fourth, don't curse the storm. You can spend your whole year angry about something that happened. Thus, all your energy is wasted in anger instead of being used for progress. Don't curse the storm. Understand it and use it. Fifth, use the storm to test your true self.

Sixth, let the storms expand the limits of your potential. Seventh, use the storm to relax and test your faith in God. Do you know why God might strip you of your dignity? In order to trust him. God will bring you back to square one in everything. Do you know the story of Job? It's a good story. The devil said to Job, I mean to God, “Let me take everything from Job and he will curse you.” God said, " Very well, go and try." I know my servant Job. This is not in the Bible. God says, " I know my servant Job."

I know this man. Why? I've already tested it. The devil said, " Okay, watch him." I will take everything. Let me take everything. " Fine, you can take everything, but don't touch his life." The man lost his farm, which was placed under seizure proceedings. All his children died. His body was afflicted with boils, sickness, and disease. All his livestock died. Everything he owned is gone. His wife was angry with him. Now, things couldn't get any worse in life. Everything is gone.

Then his wife turned to him and said, "Why don't you curse God and die?" "This god you claim to serve, look what he has allowed to happen to you." Some of you are feeling this way tonight. This is the god to whom you offered tithes and sacrifices, and to whom you went to prayer meetings. How does all this happen? Hey, storms are natural, and storms come to test your faith in God. Yes. In fact, storms will come to erode your trust in your manager. It will strip you of your trust in your company.

And return it to where it belongs, in God. And number eight, let the storms purify your relationships and habits. There are some bad habits that can only be broken by a storm. Well, I'm not talking anymore. Why did the doctor say that I have, you know, lung cancer? You've been trying to quit smoking for twenty years, and with one stroke from a doctor, you stop overnight. Boom, it's over. The storm breaks the norm. Don't curse the storm.

And number ten, let the storm push you closer to the divine materials, because you want to build your house on the right foundation, which is the word of God and a life of prayer with God. I challenge each and every one of you tonight, as we welcome this beautiful year, to prepare yourselves for some storms that will come your way. All the predictions I have seen are not positive, and I tell you, number ten, look at the storm as a messenger from God to bring glory to Himself. How could that be?

Here is the verse I always live by. Therefore, whoever thinks he is standing should be careful lest he fall. You have not experienced any trial or storm except that which is what? Common to all people. In other words, your storm is not special. The following verse, and God is faithful. When the storm comes, he says he will not allow you to experiment with what you cannot bear. Tell your neighbor that this is deep. Let me tell you what that means.

This means that everything you will face in 2012 was allowed by God because God knows you as He knows Job. Let me say it again. Whatever you face in 2012, it doesn't matter.
